provenance: Frozen 1.1.4 case contracts. Prompt clarification must preserve these acceptance criteria.

assertions.criterion: Output is a single self-contained HTML file with embedded CSS and (optionally) inline JS — no external CSS/JS frameworks; a Google Fonts import is acceptable
Productive UI surfaces follow square component anatomy while documented component-specific exceptions are preserved
Exactly one primary button on the page (the header's 'New key'); a create dialog's own Create button is the only other primary allowed, and only inside that dialog
Data table rows are multi-selectable and selection drives a batch action bar that includes Revoke and shows the selected count
Status column uses two signals — an icon/shape plus a text label, never color alone
No-data replaces the table including headers/footer; no-results preserves search/filter context; loading and error have appropriate feedback or recovery
Pagination is present for the few-hundred-row table
A Carbon token layer (CSS custom properties) and IBM Plex font stack are used, and product CSS references tokens rather than raw hex
Uses the optional standalone styling foundation coherently or explains an appropriate alternative; does not claim the CSS supplies interactive behavior
A decision log exists explaining the create-flow container choice and the density choice

cases.expected_output: A self-contained productive Carbon HTML prototype with coherent token-based styling, one page-level New key action, working selection and batch revoke, pagination, and distinguishable status. No-data replaces the table including headers/footer while useful surrounding actions remain; no-results preserves search context. Include applicable loading/error states and a short container/density rationale. Verify implemented behavior and actual contrast pairs.

assertions.criterion: Preserves readable Invoice email and Tax ID values using supported read-only controls or static labeled content
Explains disabled is not hidden, does not universally claim it is unannounced, distinguishes native disabled from ARIA disabled, and keeps read-only values legible
Rejects hiding the fields, because the user is permitted to know they exist
Specifies that the reason/upgrade path is explained outside the control (inline text, helper text, or a callout), not inside it
Describes a temporary prerequisite as a suitable disabled-state use and explains that ARIA disabled alone does not suppress activation

cases.expected_output: Prefer readable read-only controls or static labeled values with an external plan explanation and upgrade route. Distinguish native disabled, ARIA disabled, and hidden content accurately; do not claim all disabled controls disappear from screen-reader navigation or necessarily fail contrast. Focusability follows the actual element and widget contract.

assertions.criterion: Chooses productive rather than expressive motion for the task flow
Rejects diagonal paths and follows organized grid-aligned choreography
Keeps the complete staggered sequence within 500ms
Uses standard easing when the off-canvas side panel closes but remains ready to return
Includes prefers-reduced-motion and a static way to perceive state

cases.expected_output: Uses productive motion; rejects diagonal paths; staggers axes into rounded grid paths; keeps the complete row sequence within 500ms (about 20ms per row is the Carbon example); uses entrance for appearing and standard easing for a panel that remains nearby; provides reduced/static behavior.
